name: RM-Bench Code
description: The code domain split of RM-Bench (THU-KEG), evaluating reward models on their ability to discriminate subtle quality differences in code responses and resist stylistic manipulations. Tests whether code-oriented reward models reward correctness and clarity vs. superficial style properties like verbosity and formatting.
evaluation_method: reward model accuracy on subtle preference pairs for code responses; robustness to style perturbations
general_score_metric: reward model accuracy on subtle code preference pairs
typical_sota_score: ~60–75% accuracy on subtle quality pairs for code domain
reputation: ICLR 2025 Oral; part of THU-KEG/RM-Bench; reveals reward hacking patterns in code-oriented RMs; used to evaluate alignment of code reward models with actual code quality
notes: ICLR 2025 Oral. Code split of RM-Bench (THU-KEG/RM-Bench, arXiv:2410.16184). 228 instances. Each sample includes a coding prompt plus 3 chosen responses (concise, detailed plain, detailed markdown) and 3 rejected responses varying in style. Reveals whether code RMs can distinguish functionally correct concise code from verbose but incorrect solutions. Full benchmark: 1,381 total instances across chat (183), code (228), math (529), safety (441).
